docs.text: A storm moving across southeastern Canada will bring widespread rain and isolated thunderstorms to the northeast U.S. today. Lake effect showers and thunderstorms are expected downwind of the Great Lakes through Friday. Find the latest at weather.gov
A sprawling and powerful late-winter storm is about to blast the northern Plains, Midwest and Great Lakes into southeastern Canada. See how severe winter weather will be in your area:

As a 'weather bomb' develops in the eastern U.S., and tracks into Quebec, it will help draw in some of the colder Arctic air that the Prairies are feeling. This will set up the next round of lake-effect snow off of the Great Lakes. #ONwx

Just to reinforce the uncertainty here, compare the 12Z 500 mb forecasts from the new 12Z ICON and GFS models. HUGE differences in the long wave pattern. Combine with uncertainty of where 99L will consolidate, will it stay offshore or move over land and dissipate (like 12Z GFS), huge questions.

The 12z GFS goes bonkers with the LOW =970mb because the model is phasing the southern energy along the Gulf Coast with the northern eergy in the Great Lakes. No other Global model shows this solution. Both AO and NAO are strongly positive and the Pacific side teleconnections are equally bad.

Both the NAM3k and the FV3 models are really wrapping up the next system on Thurs. into Fri. Strong gradients in pressure and temperature differences will do that-like I said in an earlier post,-the active or battle zone of weather remains around the Great Lakes. #onwx #onstorm

The NAM3k is also phenomenal at p-types (except with strong low level jets where it has a warm bias). It's a great winter model. I remember about 6 years ago it picked up a lake effect streamer stretching from Lake Ontario all the way into Maine that verified. It sees things other models don't.

I'll wait for all the 12z guidance to come in to see if the trend is real. Something to watch is the slowing down of the Great Lakes trough. This could be a significant player for Atlantic Canada and Hurricane Lee.

Also watching for cape and minor storms.Ecmwf strows stronger moisture and temp advection over great lakes, GFS shows lakes acting as a boundary which is more likely.ecmwf has been over doing winter cape values, still nice to see though. Jet streams a similar in GFS/ecmwf #onwx

Surface weather map over Canada
A stalled cold front brings showers and cooler temps to southern Canada, especially near the Great Lakes. Meanwhile, western provinces enjoy clearing skies and milder conditions as Pacific high pressure builds in. #ExploreWx
I'm rooting for the ECMWF. I'm new to New England, but in the Great Lakes region it always seemed to verify better than the GFS.

As a storm system tracks over the Great Lakes & southern Ontario, the emerging trough in the West spawns low pressure somewhere in the South while high pressure builds in over Canada. How much cold/dry air & CAD in the east occurs is TBD, but it will be present in some capacity.

The GFS is similar to the ECMWF in keeping the def-zone south but does in bring a band of heavy snowfall with more substantive totals of 15-20 cm through SW ON, Northern Lake Erie and Niagara Falls. Any small shift (we're talking 20-40 km) will push this swath north/south. #ONstorm
